diagnostic_evidence.quote: This way, a strong solution of the diffusion problem is also a weak solution and the weak formulation is consistent with the strong formulation.

issues.failure_explanation:
The Nitsche consistency terms for the Dirichlet boundary must use the co-normal flux \kappa
abla u\cdot n, but the source uses 
abla u\cdot n. Integrating by parts gives an extra boundary term \int_{\Gamma_D} ((\kappa
abla u\cdot n) - (
abla u\cdot n))v\,ds, so a strong solution is not a weak solution unless \kappa=I on \Gamma_D. The linear functional and energy functional have the same missing \kappa.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert \kappa in the boundary flux terms in the bilinear form, linear functional, and energy functional (replace \nabla u\cdot n by \kappa\nabla u\cdot n in the \Gamma_D terms).
issues.overall_effect: The general formulation for variable diffusivity is inconsistent with the strong PDE. The claimed consistency and applicability to general elliptic problems with non-identity \kappa fail. The numerical examples use \kappa=I and are unaffected.
issues.title: Missing diffusivity in Nitsche boundary flux terms
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local insertion of the diffusivity tensor in the boundary terms; it preserves the method, proofs, and numerical results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for every real~$0\leq r\leq t$ it holds

issues.failure_explanation: The approximation theorem requires r\leq t. Setting r=1 and t=m requires m\geq1. The theorem only assumes m>d/2, which for d=1 allows 0.5<m<1. In that regime, u may not be in H^1 and V_{X,k} may not be in H^1, so the H^1 estimate and the negative exponent h^{m-1} are invalid.

failure_location.quote: applying first~Céa's~Lemma with~$V_h=V_{X,k}$, see~\Cref{thm:ceas-lemma}, and then the approximation error estimate from~\Cref{thm:approximation-error-estimate} with~$\tau=t=m$ and~$r=1$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis m\geq1 (or restrict to d\geq2) to Theorem 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.1 is not valid for d=1 and 0.5<m<1. The L2 theorem assumes m\geq2, so it is unaffected.
issues.title: H1 error theorem misapplies approximation theorem when m<1 in 1D
issues.why_classification: The invalid regime is a boundary case in dimension one; adding m\geq1 is a local condition that does not affect the main results in d\geq2.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Dividing by~$\coercivity-\frac{\continuity}{2}$ yields the claimed result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only yields (\alpha-\gamma/2)\|e\|^2 \leq \Delta. This implies the claimed bound only if \alpha>\gamma/2. For general coercive continuous bilinear forms, \alpha can be \leq\gamma/2, making the denominator non-positive and the inequality false. The correct bound is \|e\|^2 \leq 2\Delta/\alpha, using I(\tilde{u}_h)-I(u_h)=1/2 a(e,e).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the denominator \alpha-\gamma/2 with \alpha/2 (or 2/\alpha) and adjust Proposition 3.4 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4 are invalid when \alpha\leq\gamma/2. The error bounds with the denominator \alpha-\gamma/2 are not established.
issues.title: Inexact optimization lemma divides by possibly non-positive denominator
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line correction using an identity already in the proof; it strengthens the bound and preserves all substantive guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that the positive definite radial basis function kernel~$k\colon\Omega\times\Omega\to\R$ has an algebraically decaying Fourier transform of order~$\tau\geq m>d/2$ for some~$m\in\R$
In this example the solution is smooth and we have in particular that~$m>\tau$ for the considered values of~$\tau$.

In the first experiment we considered a~PDE with a smooth solution such that the convergence rate is limited by the smoothness of the kernel according to~\Cref{thm:a-priori-error-estimate-h1,thm:a-priori-error-estimate-l2}.

issues.failure_explanation: The table and conclusion claim the convergence rates for the case m\geq\tau (solution smoother than kernel) are according to Theorems H1 and L2. But those theorems assume \tau\geq m (kernel at least as smooth as solution). In the first numerical example, m>\tau, so the theorems do not apply. The rates for that case come from standard kernel approximation theory/superconvergence, not the paper's theorems.

failure_location.quote: The aforementioned relations regarding the regularity of the kernels together with the expected convergence rates according to~\Cref{thm:a-priori-error-estimate-h1,thm:a-priori-error-estimate-l2} are summarized in~\Cref{tab:matern-kernels-regularity}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clarify that the m\geq\tau rates are not covered by Theorems H1/L2 and that the first experiment is outside their assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The scope of the a priori error estimates is overstated. The first numerical example is outside the proven regime of the theorems.
issues.title: Scope overclaim: theorems do not cover solution smoother than kernel
issues.why_classification: A prose clarification about scope; the theorems themselves remain valid and the numerical example still illustrates expected/superconvergent behavior.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The solution is again given as~$u=g$.

issues.failure_explanation: On the sector 0<\varphi<3\pi/2, \arctan(x_2/x_1) returns a value in (-\pi/2,\pi/2), not the polar angle \varphi. Thus g as defined is not the harmonic function r^{1/\alpha}\sin(\varphi/\alpha)+1; it is not harmonic and does not solve the PDE with u=g. The claimed regularity and numerical test case are based on an incorrect definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \arctan(x_2/x_1) with atan2(x_2,x_1) or explicitly use the polar angle \varphi.
issues.overall_effect: The description and claimed regularity of the singular test case are unreliable as written. The numerical results may not correspond to the stated function.
issues.title: Singular example uses arctan instead of polar angle
issues.why_classification: The correction is a standard local replacement of \arctan with atan2; the intended harmonic function and all subsequent analysis remain valid.
